journey:warhol-last-supper.l: Various collections, including the Menil Collection, Houston, and the Andy Warhol Museum, Pittsburgh
journey:warhol-last-supper.m: Synthetic polymer paint and silkscreen ink on canvas, and drawings
journey:warhol-last-supper.noimg: © The Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts / Artists Rights Society. View works from the series through the Andy Warhol Museum.

x.summary: In his final major body of work, Warhol reworked Leonardo da Vinci's Last Supper again and again: as silkscreens, in camouflage patterns, overlaid with commercial logos, and as large hand-painted copies. Drawn from cheap reproductions of the mural, the series asks how a sacred image survives in a culture saturated with mass-produced pictures. Warhol, a quietly practising Byzantine Catholic, made some hundred works on the theme.
facts: The series was commissioned by the art dealer Alexander Iolas for an exhibition in Milan, across the street from Santa Maria delle Grazie, where Leonardo's original is painted.
The Milan exhibition opened in January 1987; Warhol died the following month, making it his last major show.
Warhol regularly attended Mass and volunteered at a homeless shelter, a side of his life that became widely known only after his death.
